title: Super Alloy Crush Locks In January 22 Steam Demo With Roguelike Brawler Action - NewsBreak
text:
By Alfredo Robelo ,
11 hours ago
Alloy Mushroom has confirmed that Super Alloy Crush will release a free demo on Steam on January 22, 2026. The date appears across the official “Demo Release Date” trailer and multiple roundup posts, which all point players to the game’s Steam page to wishlist ahead of the download opening. The demo announcement follows months of event showings, including WePlay Expo, and positions the slice as the first widely available hands-on for the community.
Super Alloy Crush is a fast-paced 2D roguelike side-scrolling brawler from Alloy Mushroom. You play as Kelly and Muu (No.02) on a cosmic treasure hunt for the planet AE-38, fighting through modular stages that remix encounters run to run. Local co-op is supported, and the tone leans into arcade immediacy with big hits, mobility options, and quick decision loops.
What to expect in the demo Trailer copy and media summaries describe a feature-forward sample that showcases high-speed combat, crowd control, and boss encounters that demand pattern reads rather than massive health bars. External previews stress a focus on elemental interactions, build variety, and momentum driven brawling, which should help players test how offense, mobility, and survival tools fit together across short runs. The aim is to deliver a vertical slice substantial enough to evaluate the game’s combat feel and pacing before Early Access.
Alloy Mushroom frames Super Alloy Crush as “Mega Man-inspired” without being a nostalgia replica. The roguelike layer adds pressure to route choices and loadout tweaks, while the brawler feel keeps encounters readable and explosive. Co-op is central rather than an afterthought, with the Steam page and announcement beats repeatedly highlighting couch or Remote Play sessions as a core use case. If you have been tracking indie action roguelikes that prize responsiveness over grind, this demo should quickly reveal whether its hit stop, recovery windows, and enemy telegraphs meet that standard.
